look_here_first: Start with the narrow straight leaves and the fruit: Buckley’s yucca makes low colonies of small rosettes with narrow whitish-threaded leaves, an unusually tall naked scape, and dry capsules pinched deeply at the middle.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small to large open colonies, mostly acaulescent or with only a short stem

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mostly straight linear leaves, usually about 0.7–1.5 cm wide

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf margins whitish/light green and filiferous, shredding into threads

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowering stalk rises far above the leaves on a long naked scape

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: erect dry dehiscent capsule deeply constricted near the middle

key_traits.label: Joey field context
key_traits.text: A Texas Observer field report documents Joey Santore pointing out Yucca constricta during a South Texas field visit. No exact reusable Joey species photo is locked yet, so the diagnostic morphology remains anchored to FNA/NPSOT rather than inferred from generic Yucca media.
